input.quote: Nothing in this Agreement authorizes MSL to use any of IBM's tangible, real or intangible property for the performance of any services contemplated hereunder on IBM Logo products or for Integration services of non-IBM Logo products related to a customer for whom Integration is being provided by IBM.
input.rationale: We reviewed the Scope of Work (§3.0), Manufacturing/Integration (§11.0), Personnel (§9.0), Licenses (§13.3), Prohibited Suppliers (§16.15) and the Integration "Restrictions and Limitations" (§14.18), plus keyword scans for "compet", "exclusive", "IBM shall not" and sourcing covenants. No non-compete, exclusivity, field-of-use or territory restriction binds IBM: the only use restrictions run against MSL (§14.18, §16.15), and the AECI expressly preserves each party's freedom to provide competitive products or services (p1491). IBM also remains free to migrate Product requirements to a competitive supplier (§9.0(e)). This meets the preferred position (no restriction on the customer's business). Note: §9.0(f) contains a time-limited non-solicit binding IBM, which is a personnel covenant rather than a non-compete/field-of-use restriction and is addressed, if at all, under the non-solicitation rule.
